title: Why Don’t Prompt-Based Fairness Metrics Correlate?
benchmark_measurement: Fluctuations in toxicity levels in model-generated text continuations for prompts mentioning different religious groups.
findings: Existing prompt-based fairness metrics showed very low correlation (Pearson correlation of 0.18) when assessing religion bias in language models. The proposed method, CAIRO, which augments prompts using other language models and selects the combination with the highest agreement, significantly increased the correlation to 0.98. This indicates that CAIRO provides a much more reliable and consistent way to measure religion bias across different fairness metrics.
